# Night 28 Briefing – Key Actions & Deadlines

| Priority | Item | Deadline / Action | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | Implement naive‑append baseline with MemGPT‑style virtual paging + periodic consolidation | **Start ASAP**; run ablation until full metrics available | Enables isolation of rewrite benefit & meets ICLR ablation demand |
| **1** | Allocate H100 GPU‑hours (2400 h/May) to ablation experiments | Use remaining budget for 5‑10× scaling of run‑time | Monitor usage ≤ 2400 h; checkpoint every 500 h |
| **2** | Review/finish workshop paper outline with Maya | **By end of day** | Draft short reply to Maya: “Draft: I’ll integrate the MemGPT baseline and add interference metrics.” |
| **3** | Prepare camera‑ready manuscript (sub. 4127) | **In 14 days** (camera‑ready due) | Ensure any new metrics from experiment are included; proof‑read |
| **4** | Update lab meeting agenda (weekly Wednesdays at 11 am) | Add agenda item: “Progress on MemGPT-based benchmark” | |

### Drafted Reply
> **To Maya**  
> “Thanks for the outline. I’ll add the MemGPT empty‑slot paging scheme as the naive‑append baseline and sketch interference metrics. Expect next version by EOD.”  

### Overnight Idea  
> **Consolidation + Paging Synergy** – Combining the periodic consolidation from the *Consolidation reduces cross‑fact interference* paper with MemGPT’s external memory paging should eliminate the 40‑item QA drop and keep token usage under budget. Use the new H100 allocation to validate this hybrid system in the rewrite‑vs‑append ablation.  

### Quick Nudges  
* *Camera‑ready* – schedule a 2‑hour writing block tomorrow.  
* *GPU quota* – set alerts for >2000 h usage.
